title: The Price of Finding a Certificate: Unsupported Pareto Points under Prefix Queries: Reproducibility Companion

creators.name: Clim, Antonio
creators.affiliation: Department of Economic Informatics and Cybernetics, Bucharest University of Economic Studies, Bucharest, Romania

description:
This reproducibility companion provides exact-arithmetic verification software, retained inputs and results, editable vector figures and claim-to-evidence maps for "The Price of Finding a Certificate: Unsupported Pareto Points under Prefix Queries". The study compares paid acquisition with the cheapest realised prefix certifying a candidate as Pareto nondominated and unsupported under nonzero nonnegative weights.

Version 1.1.0 incorporates the P57 and P58 research additions while preserving the earlier scientific code and evidence. These additions include the 87/80 upper-bound certificate and operational controls for three configurations on the triangle, a faster retrospective comparator, controlled APEX and SAT 2024 replays, sparse-support and three-alternative dimensional checks, a counterexample to universal nonnegative affine compression, exact two-anchor transfer conditions and sufficient approximation-margin controls. The 87/80 guarantee has the hypotheses stated in the accompanying manuscript, including unit row prices; it is not asserted for arbitrary tariffs. The 12/11 asymptotic optimum remains valid for the candidate-complete policy class. The unrestricted triangle optimum and convergence remain open.

The new dimensional checks use exact rational arithmetic, with separately labelled floating-point SciPy/HiGHS cross-checks. Finite computational controls do not establish universal theorems by themselves. Three-alternative geometric verification in arbitrary dimension does not imply a universal lossless reduction of paid observations to two dimensions. The experiments do not establish measured monetary, energy or deployed-service benefits. Internal independently implemented checks are author-side AI-assisted controls, not external peer review or proof-assistant verification.

The APEX replays reuse APEX Dataset: Testbed Traces and Evaluation Results, version 1.0 (https://doi.org/10.3217/3dhx0-2k125); the associated article is https://doi.org/10.1145/3770918. Source bytes, attribution and licence notices already present in version 1.0.0 are retained. SAT 2024 derived results use the official results at https://satcompetition.github.io/2024/. The original SAT ZIP/CSV is not redistributed; acquisition instructions and its frozen checksum are supplied.

Licences apply by component: BSD-3-Clause covers the author's covered code and executable configuration; CC BY 4.0 covers the author's covered documentation, result tables and figures, within his rights. Original APEX data and DejaVu fonts retain their third-party terms and notices. LICENSING.md and LICENSE_SCOPE.json define the scope. The manuscript, supplementary manuscript, cover letter and private submission materials are not included or relicensed. No GitHub Actions workflow is included.
